utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom. The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Welcome back to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony yesterday still applies today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan is continuing her examination in chief. You have the floor, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good afternoon to Your Honours and to the Defence and everyone else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We left off yesterday with you demonstrating some of your findings using the detailed images of the document that you had captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we can go back to those images, which is 65 ter 7527. And if we could turn to page 2, please. If we can actually just keep it as it is for the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you see, on the left there, there's some handwritten notations?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Who made those notations?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made those notations.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what it says? It's somewhat faint there.

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, on top, 00696610. And at the bottom it says row 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to the attendance roster itself, which is P1754, page 3 of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'd ask, if it's possible this time, to display the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we've been looking at the excerpts of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we -- yeah, could we flip to page 3 in the B/C/S, which I think is also page 3 in the English version. Sorry, it must be page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps it -- I think it would be sufficient to have the column 1 and 2 of the English version on the screen so that the B/C/S version could be enlarged a bit, if that is technically possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was referring to the English version. Perhaps we can move both a bit to the right. We could make the right-hand side of the screen smaller and enlarge the left-hand side. Is that possible? Exactly. Sorry for my proposal. It takes some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, it's a great proposal. Actually, we can see now much better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that sufficient for your purposes, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, if we could just scroll down the English version so we can see the very top of that page -- sorry, scroll up. Yeah. Okay. Just to put into context what we were looking at yesterday, we're looking row 1, and that is -- the name in that row is Miomir Jasikovac. And as Your Honours may recall, that's the Lieutenant Miomir Jasikovac who was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade military police company unit. And we were looking, as you can see here, this is the roster, attendance roster, for July 1995, which is recorded on the top right-hand corner, and the image -- the zoomed-in image we were looking at the end of the session yesterday was for the days marked the 14 and 15 column, which is the 14th and 15th of July. Now, we're just going to take a look at one more example of a zoomed-in image, and that is at page 2 of 65 ter 7527. And actually if we could just -- if we haven't yet switched to that image, we would be looking at rows 4 and 5, which are recorded as Nada Stojanovic and Goran Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Hasan kindly speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 3 of 65 ter 7527.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, again there's some handwritten notations on this image. Could you just tell us what those notations are?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The upper notation is the evidence number 0069 -- I will just get it -- 6610. The image here is quite difficult to see because it's tilted too much. And the second -- the first row is row 4 and the second row shown is row 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what we see in this image here?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we see in this image is that in column 14 we have an original entry of an O in row 4 and row 5, and there are still remnants of the -- of the pencil left there which makes it almost -- well, visible by naked eye almost, and this is an enhanced image of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, Your Honours, the original attendance roster is with the Court Officer if you'd like to take a look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, what technique did you use to see these and to capture this image?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This image is captured, I believe, by oblique lighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we could now turn to your expert report, 65 ter 642.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we have page 4 displayed, please. And I believe it's the same page number for the English and the B/C/S versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what it is that's recorded in this segment of your report?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this segment of my report I have listed where we have encountered changes. In the upper segment, it's just a summation of some of the changes which we've encountered in the document, but we haven't specified where these changes were because they were not really in the questions asked. In the lower part, we specified the changes which we found in relation to the letter O and the name "Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And aside from the rows and the columns that you've recorded here where you've found the letter O, did you find any other Os in the document?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Besides that, we didn't find any other original O entries in the document, as far as I recall. This is -- these are the only O entries we found in the document, which had been erased. Of course, in the document there are other Os, but not the ones -- we were looking for the erased Os.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in this portion here, I see that you report on not only the erased letter Os but also erased letter Rs that you seem to have found in column 15, which is the entry for July 15. Why was it that you were reporting on the letter R?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were reporting on the letter R because there seemed to be some relation between the Os and the Rs. In most of the rows where we encountered a letter O had been erased, also a letter R had been erased in the column next to it. So we thought this may be interesting information for the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was that something that the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY asked you to look for?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can just turn the page now to page 5 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, the first sentence here, in English, reads: "Whenever the overwriting has been done in pencil with very little pressure and expertly erased, the original writing cannot be established." What is overwriting?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Overwriting here is a wrong translation of what -- of the Dutch version of the report. In the Dutch version we said "whenever entries have been done in pencil," so we are emphasizing more the original entries here and not the overwriting itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And there's a reference in the English translation to "expertly erased." What is meant by "expertly erased"?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Expertly erased is that, well, someone takes the time to really erase it properly with -- and that can be done with a normal eraser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anything else that you noted from the English translation of the report that you wish to correct at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JAN DE KOEIJER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some difficulty in the translation of the method "infrared reflection" on page 3. However, I've already discussed this method yesterday, so I don't -- I'm not sure if a true correction is necessary in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I would then offer into evidence 65 ter 642, which is the expert report of Mr. de Koeijer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This report will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 642 shall be assigned Exhibit P2595. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in addition to that, we have gone through all the close-up images in the collection that Mr. de Koeijer provided to us, and I would offer those images into evidence. And they bear the 65 ter number 7527.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This collection of images will be received as an exhibit, too. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. Mr. Tolimir had trouble hearing the interpretation. However, everything is all right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I take it now you receive proper interpretation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It's fine now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Hasan has moved for accepting the document 65 ter number 7527, which will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7527 shall be assigned Exhibit P2596. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, those were all my questions for the witness during my direct. I have a very brief submission to make, but I will do that at the conclusion of this witness's testimony, and it just relates to other evidence in relation to this military roster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, you may now commence your cross-examination. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Peace unto this house and may this day of proceedings and the whole trial end in keeping with God's will, not with mine. I would like to welcome Mr. de Koeijer and thank him for come to testify in this trial. The Defence has no questions for this witness. Thank you, Mr. President. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Hasan, in that case, I take it that you don't have any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. de Koeijer, the Chamber would like to thank you that you were able to provide us with your expertise and your report and your testimony yesterday and today. You are now free to return to your normal activities. Thank you very much again. Now you are free to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, the original documents we have received this morning, they should be given back to the Prosecution. Ms. Hasan, you wanted to submit something. You have floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, as we wait for the next witness to come in and for Mr. Vanderpuye to make his way down to the courtroom, I just wanted to remind you of some of the witnesses that you have heard and whose evidence is part of the trial record that relates to the Zvornik Brigade military police roster and the findings of Mr. de Koeijer; namely, Nebojsa Jeremic, Stanoje Bircakovic, Dragoje Ivanovic, Milorad Bircakovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down. We would like to have the names properly recorded. Perhaps you could repeat the third name.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. Dragoje Ivanovic. The fourth name is recorded correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please wait until we see the correct name. There it is. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: PW-57, PW-58, PW-59, and the evidence of PW-60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that Mr. Tomasz Blaszczyk is the next witness. After the arrival of Mr. Vanderpuye, he should be brought into the courtroom. Good afternoon, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone. Mr. President, I'm not sure what our position is with respect to the cross-examination of Mr. Blaszczyk who is entering the courtroom as our next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This was a matter that I raised with Mr. Gajic in advance of his testimony, and I didn't hear back from the Defence with respect to that issue. So I assume that it's a matter that's being resolved or will be resolved in accordance with my communication with Mr. Gajic which suggested that if the Defence so requires, that they, perhaps, will make an application to the Trial Chamber to postpone Mr. Blaszczyk's cross-examination. We are aware of the Trial Chamber's order from July, I believe it was 19th, in respect of our application to expand the scope of Mr. Blaszczyk's testimony, and in relation to the addition of another witness whom, pursuant to the order, the Trial Chamber indicated should be called as the last witnesses in the Prosecution's case. Unfortunately, because of scheduling issues and the availability of restrictions, I would say, or limitations on some of our other witnesses, that has become, I would say, impossible to do, although we've tried to. So I'm prepared to go forward, and I'd leave it to Mr. Gajic to let us know what the Defence's position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir or Mr. Gajic, do you want to respond? Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence will not delay the cross-examination of Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for this information. There is no objection to proceed now with Mr. Blaszczyk's evidence. Welcome back, Mr. Blaszczyk, to the courtroom and to this trial. You have been here several times already and testified on other matters. Now, in relation to a different matter. However, the affirmation to tell the truth, the oath you made at the beginning of the first day of your testimony, still applies today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. And good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, your examination-in-chief, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And welcome back again. Your qualifications and experience are all on the record, so I will not go back into that. Today we're here to talk about a collection of evidence that is in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor, so let's just get right to it. Are you familiar with a collection of evidence that the Office of the Prosecution has referred to in this trial as the Pecanac collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us a little bit about how it is that this collection of evidence came into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November 2009, the Office of the Prosecutor asked the authorities of Republic of Serbia to conduct a search of the premises belonging to Mr. Dragomir Pecanac, the former VRS officer. And this search was conducted on the 2nd of December, 2009, and during the search several items were seized from the house of Mr. Pecanac, including some CDs, a computer, and some documents. It was 2nd of December, 2009. Prosecutor Office, on our request, we received first in January 2010 the copy, scanned copy, of the document seized at Mr. Pecanac's accommodation, and later on, I believe, I think it was March 2010 we received also a copy of the hard drive of the computer seized from Mr. Pecanac's accommodation on the 2nd of December, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually, I think I should apply to the Trial Chamber first. This is, Your Honour, a document that's not part of our 65 ter list. It's designated 765 ter 7522. And it relates to a number of items that were the subject of the seizure. In fact, it's a certificate thereof which I would like to present to the Trial Chamber. I don't know whether the Defence has any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to greet Mr. Vanderpuye and Mr. Blaszczyk. The Defence has no objection to any evidence presented by the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to move into private session just for a brief moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness should be brought into the courtroom again, please. And we all should try to decide case-by-case how to proceed in open or in private session, if it's necessary, but now I think everybody is aware of the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please sit down, Mr. Blaszczyk. Our apologies for this interruption and the delay, but now we are continuing. We are in open session. Mr. Vanderpuye, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think I was just about to call up 65 ter 7522. If we could have that in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We have it now in e-court in both B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But I would like to add --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add this document to the 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is confirmation of -- this is said record -- seized record from the search conducted at the 2nd of December, 2009, at the house of Mr. Pecanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what does it -- what does it show? I see, here, that there are a number of items indicated here. Are these the items that were confiscated and turned over to the ICTY, that is, the OTP?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Most of these items were handed over to the ICTY, to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go, please, to page 3 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the bottom of this page -- one moment, we're getting there in the B/C/S. At the bottom of the page, we can see that there is a pair of signatures. And are you familiar with either of these signatures?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the left-hand-side signature. It's the signature of Dragomir Pecanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you tell us, just briefly, how you're familiar with the signature of Mr. Pecanac.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had opportunity to review some documents signed by Mr. Pecanac from the period of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We'll take a look at those in a little while.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I may, at this time, Mr. President, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7522 shall be assigned Exhibit P2597. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, in this certificate that we've just looked at --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go back to page 1 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- it indicates that a search was carried out. It gives the address and the time as 11.30 on the 2nd of December, 2009. Do you know whether or not any member of the OTP or maybe even the ICTY was involved in carrying out or conducting this search?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not. No one from ICTY, from OTP, participated in this search.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the very last page of this document, it indicated here -- or it indicates, rather, that an investigating judge will be notified of the temporary confiscation of items. And are you aware of any proceedings that followed the confiscation of these items, as indicated in this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the procedurals from Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, the investigation judge should approve the seizure, should approve also the items seized from particular citizen, in this case Mr. Pecanac, and issuing the order, or whatever, information or just confirmation -- to, that's it, to Mr. Pecanac in this case, that these items in particular were seized from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I would like to show you is 65 ter 7523.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would apply also to add this particular exhibit to the Prosecution's 65 ter list. This relates to the question that I've just asked Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it from the previous answer of Mr. Tolimir that there is no objection. It may be added to the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could -- we do have it in e-court already.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us basically what it is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document dated 12th February, 2010. This is a kind of the record from interview conducted by -- by MUP guys, by MUP people from Republic of Serbia, with Dragomir Pecanac, related to seizure of the documents and also to the seized material.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go -- I think it should be to the second page in both documents. I'm sorry, we should stay on the first page in the B/C/S. It's just under the indication of his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the page, and we'll see that under -- right under the word "statement," or the caption "statement," it indicates the documents that were seized from me pursuant to a record number 03/4-3-1, number 230-9894, and it says 09, on 2nd December, 2009. And he says that these documents were seized from him and he'd been collecting them for years, for many years; you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does this refer to the search that you've just testified about, the document that we've just seen?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. It refers to the search conducted on this particular date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we go to the last page, I think it will be page 3 in the English, page 2 in the B/C/S, we can see that the document is signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it also refers to the date of completion as February 12 at 1600 hours and also indicates that the party took a copy of his statement; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to also tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7523 shall assigned Exhibit P2598. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. Blaszczyk --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I notice one mistake in the translation. We have the correct page on the screen. It says: "The party, Dragomir Pecanac," and in English it says "signed." However, there is no signature in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That is correct. I see that in the translation, and I believe I see that in the document. The document does not appear to reflect a signature of Mr. Pecanac but reflects signatures of the other individuals there, Danijela Antic, Srdan Citakovic, and Dalibor Radakovic. I would still tender the document. I think it's still admissible. Nevertheless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is already received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And hopefully I will have a chance to address the party indicated, Mr. Pecanac, with that -- with this document as well. I have an indication that it's the break time, and maybe it's a good point to take it, since I'm about to move to a different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. -- sorry, Judge Mindua has a question in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vanderpuye, I don't know whether you responded to the objection made by the Defence with regard to the lack of a signature by Mr. Pecanac, because on the document I have before me it says that he admits having seen the minutes and the items seized and he signs, but there is no signature. Generally, when someone refuses to sign, it states that the person has not signed for such and such a reason, but here nothing is said. How can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye will have the opportunity to put this question to Mr. Pecanac if he did sign it or what would be the reason why he didn't sign it when he appears as a witness in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, hopefully I will have that opportunity, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, have you any idea about the reason why this document was not signed by Mr. Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no information why this document is not signed by Mr. Pecanac. I can only guess why not. Regarding this interview conducted on 12th February, 2010, by the colleagues from Serbia MUP, Mr. Pecanac also -- I think this interview is also mentioned in interview conducted by investigation -- Investigative Judge Mr. Dilparic in March the same year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We must have the first break now, and we will resume quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I see you on your feet, Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just briefly. As promised, the Defence has filed responses to three Prosecutor's submissions, so I believe that there are no pending replies to any Prosecutor's submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We appreciate that. Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Blaszczyk. I had asked you before whether or not the OTP or the ICTY was involved in the execution of the search of Mr. Pecanac, as you may recall. Can you tell us, was the search undertaken as a result of a request by the OTP to search Mr. Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the search was undertaken as a result of a request of OTP. But physically OTP members did not participate in the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall, roughly, when that request was made relative to when the search was actually carried out? About how long in advance was it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was -- we requested for the search about two weeks before the search was actually conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you 65 ter 7536, but before I do, let me ask leave of the Trial Chamber to add this document to the Prosecution's 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would note, Mr. President, also, the document wasn't on the exhibit list that I provided Mr. Gajic, but I've asked for leave to add it because I think it's quite responsive to the question that was put by His Honourable Judge Mindua concerning or bearing upon the significance of Mr. Pecanac's or the lack thereof of his signature on the document that I showed previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can I take it again that there is no objection to add this document to the 65 ter exhibit list?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Leave is granted. Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I can just show you this document very briefly, Mr. Blaszczyk. There we have it. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what -- what it is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a record of interview conducted by Judge Milan Dilparic with Dragomir Pecanac regarding the seized documents. And in this interview one investigator and one lawyer from OTP also took the part, but mostly judge asked the question of Mr. Dragomir Pecanac. This interview was conducted on 31st March, 2010, also on our request.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to show you, if we could just --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just move briefly to page 7 in the English, and I think the corresponding page in the B/C/S will be page -- page 5. Page 6 in the B/C/S, sorry. The next one. And here -- we can see here, specifically, that Mr. Pecanac indicates here that he submitted everything that he had, referring to the period from 2nd December 2009 through 12 December 2010 following the search that occurred. And if we could go to page 11 in the English and page 9, I believe, in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He refers also to some documents, some 25 items. Do you see that at the top of the screen there, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know what he's referring to? Are those the items you referred to in -- that he turned over in March, or are these other items?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In here Mr. Pecanac's referring to the items handed over by him on the 4th of March, 2010, to Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are these -- these are separate items than the ones that were the result of the search in December of 2009; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. They are different items, not the same which were seized on the 2nd December.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did the OTP receive these items as well?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I won't need this on the screen at the moment, and I'm not planning to tender it, unless the Trial Chamber would like to receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And let me ask you a couple of questions about -- about the documents. First, in terms of the material that was received as a result of the search, can you tell us what form that was in?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, we received this material in the form of DVDs or CDs, relevant DVDs, exactly relevant DVDs, and with a scanned document or a copy of the document seized from Mr. Pecanac on the 2nd December 2009. And then, I think, in March we received also one DVD containing material from the hard drive or the computer belonged to Mr. Pecanac and also seized during the search conducted on the 2nd December, 2009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, you said you received a certain number of DVDs. How many did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, all together there was -- there were 11 DVDs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That was what I wanted to have on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was this material received electronically, that is, in the form of digital data, as in DVDs, as well as physical copies, hard copies, of the documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are referring to documents or materials seized from Mr. Pecanac, we received this material in electronical [sic] copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us, in terms of the chain of custody, what was done with that material once it was received? First, let's start with where it was received.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first material was handed over to our field office in Belgrade, ICTY field office. And then from ICTY field office, material was taken to The Hague by one of the investigators. And a team dealing with this particular case received this material just the following day or the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when the material was received, was it processed in accordance with the protocol that you previously testified to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The material we received, in fact, was -- we started the process here in ICTY, in The Hague, after fall -- yeah. Let me explain, Your Honour, because when we started to review the material received from Belgrade field office, at one point we discovered that this material contains also quite sensitive material. I mean, privileged Defence material, and we immediately - after discovering this issue - we informed our lawyers from our team that such material exists in these DVDs or CDs and immediately we were ordered -- we were told to stop reviewing material. And I believe it was Mr. McCloskey who set up the protocol for us which we should follow in our just reviewing, in future, this material. And following this protocol, we were also tasked to review the material to index the material, but we should skip all the material which would have been potential Defence material.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was the -- was the material itself documented, MFI'd, given an index number or an ERN number?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, receiving these 11 DVDs, we selected the material which could be potential evidence for us and also selected these privileged material, potential Defence material. We put in this material for -- to another DVD, but we processed the material without this potential privileged material, and we MFI'd this material and we submitted to Evidence Unit. It was scanned. In following process, it was scanned and put in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say it was scanned, I take it you are referring to the digital data that was on the CDs?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So that material would have been printed out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be printed out because Evidence Unit has little bit -- I would say, you know, we would policy that material. We should print out the material and submit them in hard copies. The material was printed out, as far as I remember, at that time from these 11 DVDs we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And just bear with me one moment.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you were going to continue?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my recollection, but I can be wrong: It is possibility that because of the quality of material we ask evidence unit just to electronically stamp the material from DVDs, but right now I am not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what kind of material, digital material, is this, were these text files, were these photograph files, were they PDFs, or a mix of that kind of media?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This material -- I mean, the DVDs contains various material. It was PDF files, photographs, scanned documents, photographed documents, this type of material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Word -- Word -- sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Word documents as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, please look at the record, page 42, line 11, the first word. I didn't hear you saying this word. Please correct it. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I said digital data, if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is what I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could show you 65 ter 7535.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is another document that bears on the -- the nature of the material that was received but was not part of the Prosecution's original 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To shorten the procedure, if there would be an objection, I think Mr. Tolimir would raise his hand. There is no objection, therefore it will be -- leave is granted to add it to the 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think we have it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And this is a document from the Ministry of the Interior, from Republic of Serbia. Are you familiar with this document, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it relates to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document related to the hard drive; in fact, to the contents of the hard drive seized from Mr. Pecanac in December 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us, in terms of the material that was seized, was all of the material in the form - that is the digital form - the forms that you've indicated previously?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this material was in digital form.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were any of these forms -- any of these -- this media recovered from deleted files, or were they all files that were existing immediately on the hard drive itself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the analyst number, special unit of Serbian MUP, some of the files were recovered from deleted files.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were those files among the files that were printed and processed here at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean these deleted files, I don't think so because most of the deleted files - it was Word files - related, rather, to the Defence, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you say "related to the Defence," you're referring to the potentially privileged materials?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. We tried to avoid to read these documents, and we didn't process this stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we have here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we have also Serbian MUP document hard disk analysis report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this what you were referring to just a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. More information of this analysis, I believe, is on the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could take a look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here we can see that it is signed by a special police officer, and it indicates, as you testified a moment ago, that there were numerous Word documents that had been found. And it indicates also --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, kindly speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It indicates also that some of them had been overwritten.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. But it also indicates that they could be reopened; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is correct. They could be reopened using the special software.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7535 shall be assigned Exhibit P2599. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, what Id like to take you to or ask you about, Mr. Blaszczyk, is, have you had a chance to review these documents, that is, some of the documents that were recovered during this search, and compare them against other documents in the collections of the Office of the Prosecutor relevant to this particular case?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I had a chance to review the contents of this drive, hard drive, and also the contents of the previous CDs or DVDs, and especially hard drive contains a lot of documents in different format. It was PDF document -- all together it was about 11.000 [Realtime transcript read in error "1100"] documents in this hard drive, including about, as far as I remember, about 3.000 JPEG files and about 3.000 PDF files. Most -- we realised that most of these especially JPEG files, which depicted the scanned document or photographed documents from the war period, we never seen before. We tried to -- I will try to explain the situation, because, as I said, there was about 3.000 JPEG files of the document. In fact, one JPEG file was one page of the document, and these JPEG files or the pages were not organised together. We had to find a way how to put it together, how to collect these pieces together. For example, if document has about five pages, it could be five different JPEG files. Unfortunately, we had problem to -- in fact, logistical problem to went through all these files and just to find the proper page belonging to the proper document. But we managed. Finally we did it. And finally, I believe it was October that we finished this process.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Having concluded the process, Mr. Blaszczyk, can you give us an estimate of approximately how many -- I think you have already. You said there were about 1100 [sic] documents that were found in this material; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were more documents. I mean more files. But, yes, about -- quite big collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you 65 ter 7505, which is a document we have on our 65 ter list, and ask you if you recognise it. Now, you may notice at the top of the English translation of this document there are remarks that don't appear on the B/C/S. And if we go to the very top so we can all see, you will see that it's a translation of a document with an ERN number of 0529-7001. And on the left of the screen we can see a document with an ERN number of 0704-8796. Have you had a chance to compare this document, that is, the B/C/S document on the left, with the original document of which -- to which this English translation corresponds?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I had opportunity to review these two documents, to compare these two documents. It's more or less the same documents, but the documents we see in original language in B/C/S, on the left-hand side of this monitor, this is documents recovered from hard drive of Mr. Pecanac's computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember -- first, I remember this document, and then it's quiet easy for me because I, looking at the ERN number, I see that this is the range which documents from hard drive of Mr. Pecanac were Pecanac stamped.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is of the ERN range beginning with 0704?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. I think it was even before 0703, but following 0704.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you've indicated that this was from the hard drive.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's correct. Looking at the ERN number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go, just briefly, to the next page in -- well, the B/C/S, and we can go to the last page, I suppose, in the English, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us about what we have here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the bottom of this page, I am referring to this original page, the quality is maybe not the best one, but we see with the signature -- I believe this is signature of Mr. Pecanac, and on the right-hand side we see a red stamp. This red stamp, according to my knowledge, according to information I got, this is stamp used in the Main Staff of Army of Republika Srpska in Crna Rijeka, and -- I think in Crna Rijeka. Why I came to this conclusion, because -- yes. I interviewed personally one man who worked in the Crna Rijeka compound as cryptographer. He described the stamp as used by them when they were processing documents received or sent. His name is Dragan Stokic. And also another cryptographer from the same unit, his unit, who served in Crna Rijeka confirmed that it was the stamp and the way how they processed the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I'd like to do, just so that we can show the Trial Chamber, very briefly, is to pull up the B/C/S version of this document -- of the translation we see here on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I believe that the ERN number for that is -- I think it's 5308, but just give me one second. I'm sorry, it's 3803, 65 ter 3803. Yes, I'd like the B/C/S page to stay on the screen, that's for 65 ter 7505. And if we could just go to the first page of the B/C/S on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And we can see, first, a couple of very obvious differences. One is the type.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you comment on that, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's visible here that these documents from my left-hand side is -- was typed with -- using a type writer. And documents on my right-hand side was printed out from the teleprinter. If I can, Your Honour, I would like to comment something. I referred just a few second or few minutes ago to one of the cryptographer I interviewed personally, and he explained me the procedure how they send the documents. He says that they used to receive documents prepared by the office of the Army of Republika Srpska from the Main Staff, it could be handwritten documents and could be also documents typed on the typewriter. They're supposed to receive these documents, they're supposed to put the stamp over their documents when these documents were received and sent out to the recipients. On the right-hand side, I see that this is probably document received from one of the recipients mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can also see in the photocopy of the document in the B/C/S on the right-hand-side screen, that is, of 65 ter 3803, an indication, a number, 5632. And -- but we don't see that on the copy on the left-hand side of the screen, which is 65 ter 7505.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, could you please repeat the number which you read into the record because it is not properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. It was 65 ter 3803.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here we can see some handwritten notes on either of these documents that are not reflected in the other.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how does that occur, to your understanding, or how can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, as I said, you know, these documents from the left-hand side was sent from the Main Staff, and the document on the right-hand side was received by one of the recipients. I think it is the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade as -- if I see correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the second page, please, of both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You will see that the one on the left bears two stamps, a blue stamp and a red stamp; and the one on the right bears no stamp. Now, you've indicated that you had a conversation with a cryptographer who explained the process, and does that relate to the red stamp or the blue stamp that appears on the document on the left, 65 ter 7505?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this relates to the red stamp on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what is your understanding, if any, of the blue stamp on the -- near the signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is stamp of military post.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And having reviewed these two documents, did you notice any discrepancies or differences, I should say, in the text of the document itself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in the text nothing except the signature. We have here a type -- information that this document was to type -- on the left, on this left document, left-hand-side documents, we see that this document was signed for Colonel Zdravko Tolimir, and signature -- I believe this is signature of Dragomir Pecanac. And on the right-hand-side document, we see only typed name of Colonel Zdravko Tolimir. We don't have a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Beneath the signature we can see what appear to be a set of initials, DP/LJS, and we see that also on the typewritten document. Did you speak to the cryptographer about that, or what is your understanding of what that signifies?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is signature of the people who draft this document. And other signature -- sorry, initials, this is initials of the man who typed over this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me move to a different document. Mr. President, I would like --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- to tender these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, what do you think does "DP" depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this is the initials of the man, but I don't know which one. First, who draft this document; and second one should be that one who typed this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But you don't know whom it stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Off the top of my head, no, I don't remember. I should compare the list of the people who used to work for this organ. Dragan -- DP could be Dragan -- Dragomir Pecanac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Both documents will be received. First, 65 ter 705. I correct myself: 65 ter 7505.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7505 shall be assigned Exhibit P2600.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then the other document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And 65 ter document 3803 shall be assigned Exhibit P2601. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show you, Mr. Blaszczyk, 65 ter 7506 [Realtime transcript read in error "7056"].

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I would like to do is to go to the second page in the B/C/S, which corresponds to the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is this a document that was part of the collection of documents that were seized from Mr. Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is document -- one of the documents from the Pecanac collection, but I see, looking at this ERN number, of course, that these documents was -- was on CD we received first from these relevant CDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so those CDs, I take it, were processed separately from the documents that have an ERN in the range of 0703 through 0704, beginning with those numbers?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The CD, these relevant CDs, were processed; I believe it was finished by end of January 2010. But with hard drive we had to work until October 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so the documents that were on the CD are denoted in the ERN range 0554. Is that how you know what's what?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. And I just -- I recognised the ERN range.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is to pull up 65 ter 750 -- 7506 - is that what I have? - 7525, I'm sorry. And I would like to keep the B/C/S of 7506 up on the screen so that we can compare them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think on page 52, line 15, it should read 65 ter 7506.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to compare these two documents, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I compared these two documents. As I said, these documents on the left-hand side, this is documents from Pecanac collection. But looking at this document from my right-hand side, I see this is documents from so-called Drina Corps collection. I testified about this collection some time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the content of these two documents, have you had a chance to review that? And if you have, are they the same?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had the chance to review these documents and the contents is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is to take you to the last page of both of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That should be page 7 in the B/C/S on the left, that is, 65 ter 7 -- sorry, 7506. And then it should be page 2 on the right-hand, which is 7525.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about this, here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we see, this left-hand-side document has been signed by military prosecutor Lieutenant Colonel Nebojsa Supic. And this document on the right-hand side is not signed, it's also typed, military prosecutor Lieutenant Colonel Nebojsa Supic, but it's not signed, these documents, by him. I don't see clearly who signed the other one, I mean the stamp and the signature on the left-hand side of document from Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can also see that -- well, the document on the right, 7525, bears two signatures, and on the left there appears to be only one. And is that because -- well, if you're able, can you explain how that is or why that is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this document, the second one with two signatures, one typed and another one typed also and a signature, was prepared -- in fact, it was just copy of this previous documents, and this is why these two people signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Lastly, you may have noticed that the script is actually different between the two documents; that is, one being in the Cyrillic script and the other being in the Latinic script.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, but the contents is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And were -- how were you able to make that comparison?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just compared what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender these documents as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, both -- first Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think for the sake of clarification it would be perhaps necessary for the Trial Chamber and maybe even the witness to see the translation of 7525, the last page, where two names are indicated, one signature, one stamp; and on the right-hand side, there is only a name. I think that will clear up a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We could have, in addition to the two B/C/S versions, the English translation on the screen. The last page of it, please. Mr. Vanderpuye, do you want to put a question in relation to the English translation to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I suppose I will. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you seen this particular designation before, Mr. Blaszczyk, that is, the certification of the -- of the original?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is translation of these document from Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, before you continue, I have to interrupt for a moment.
