On behalf of all those present, I would like to thank her for her contribution for our common work and wish you all the best, Ms. Naili, for your future career and personally all the best. Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Having seen these certification, does this change your view as to the parity in comparing these two documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that this is, document on the left-hand side, signed only by -- signed by army prosecutor is the original one, and on the right-hand side I think we have translation -- we have translation here. This is a certified copy of the original we see on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to tender these documents. I'm not sure if they've been received yet. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, not yet. 65 ter 7506 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2602. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And also 65 ter 7525.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2603. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you now, Mr. Blaszczyk, if I could, 65 ter 7508. This is a document that we can see here from the Ministry of Interior Republika Srpska, dated 18 July 1995, from Deputy Minister Tomislav Kovac, and it concerns the sort of distribution of work between military police and MUP civilian police concerning check-points in the republic. Have you had a chance to review this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about it in terms of its form and content and whether or not you've compared it to any other documents in the collections of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is document signed by minister of -- Deputy Minister of Interior Tomislav Kovac. I am referring to the document on the left-hand side, the original one. And on the top of these documents, we have handwritings here, and signature and initials. As I see here, and I believe the initials on the left side with -- used by black pen are initials of -- I believe that they are initials of Colonel Beara, and initials on the right side with blue pen, we see here blue pen and also handwritings, I believe this is handwritings and initials of General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of questions. First, how do you know or what makes you think that the initials in the black pen at the top of the screen, under the lettering A/A, that those are the initials of Ljubisa Beara, Colonel Ljubisa Beara?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, I had opportunity to review a lot of documents, and I met these initials before. And I believe this is Colonel Beara initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you referred to the initials of General Tolimir as well, and you've indicated that those initials are in the blue pen on the right-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is correct. I refer to the initials now very visible on the screen as the initials of General Tolimir and his handwriting as well. I would like to mention that his initials and these initials, not particularly from this document, from other documents and handwritings, have been shown to various witnesses and they recognise handwritings and they believe also that the handwritings and initials are initials and handwritings of General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I would like to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could display it side by -- well, actually, there's a better idea. Let's go down to the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I want to show you the stamp and signature here. Are you familiar with this particular signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not very familiar with signature, but I believe that reflects the typed name here, it being Tomislav Kovac signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And let me show you now also 65 ter 2590.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to have the B/C/S only in e-court. Just the B/C/S -- side by side with the B/C/S for 65 ter 7508. The number should be 2590. All right. I need to correct myself. It should be 65 ter 7526, and I'm comparing it against 65 ter 7508. I apologise. Thanks. We have it now. And if we could just make the one on the left a little bit smaller so we can compare them -- well, we'll leave it -- let's leave it like it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here you can see the signatures. And they appear to be similar but different. Are you able to explain -- explain that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would try, at least, Your Honour. On the document from the left-hand side, we see the stamp of -- the stamp of minister of interior of RS and signature -- what I believe is signature of Tomislav Kovac, deputy minister. And if we look at the document -- and this document was -- this is from Pecanac collection. If you look at the document form the right-hand side on the screen here, I see this document, I compared the ERN number with this document - I know that it was seized in one of the police station, I believe, in Banja Luka some time ago - and this is exactly the same document -- the copy of the same document of the -- I would say an original of the -- which we have on the left-hand side. And regarding the signature, it looks similar like Tomo Kovac signature, Tomislav Kovac's signature, but I don't see a stamp here. Whether it has been signed by him later on, or the copy, I have no explanation. But definitely this document was seized from MUP building in, I think, in Banja Luka some time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say that it's an exact copy of -- well, they are exact copies of one another, you're referring to the typewritten text in addition to the handwritten text or just the typewritten text?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to typewritten text. You know, if you look at the number of these documents, what is mentioned here is also the same one, it's P/92/95. Comparing the text, it's exactly the same one. But I'm referring to typewritten texts, not handwritings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I would like to move to a different document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I would like to tender both of these documents as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 65 ter 7508 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2604. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As well as 65 ter 7526.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2605. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just bear with me one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show you 65 ter 7510. Here we can see we have a document from the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, and it says the organ for security and intelligence, and it's directed to the Main Staff, among other units. The security and intelligence administration of the Main Staff. If we go to the last page, the second page of both documents, we'll see that it's issued under the name of Zoran Carkic, the chief of security for the brigade. In part, if we go to page 1 of this document, you'll see that it talks about or refers to Muslim forces in Zepa that have been crushed into small or large groups now trying to break the encirclement in all directions. And that's basically in the first paragraph following the indication of movement of enemies -- of the enemy that were crushed. If we go to page 2, we will see a reference there to a number of men that have surrendered to the VJ and the Serbian MUP. It indicates that a number of them had been registered in the sector of Crni Potok and they were attempting to cross over the right bank. First, can you tell us, in context, what this particular document concerns?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is kind of intelligence report about the Muslim population or Muslim forces near Zepa or Zepa enclave. This document was prepared by the head of security organ from Rogatica Brigade, Captain Zoran Carkic, and was sent by him also to security department and intelligence department of the main headquarters of Army of Republika Srpska. As we see here on the document, there is a stamp, also described by the people who are working in communication, that the stamp used in the Main Staff. And referring to this other purple stamp, the colour is visible here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you able to compare the content of this document, that is, its subject matter, to any other material independent of the material from the Pecanac collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I -- yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just before we get there, I will note just that the ERN range on this document falls within the range starting with 0704. Does that correspond to the material that was processed as part of the Pecanac collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is correct. This is material that is part of the Pecanac collection. By -- but the material from this document is -- comes from his computer, his hard drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you P345.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, are you tendering the last document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This confidential document shouldn't be broadcast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what we have here on the screen, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is intercept of the conversation between VRS officer and officers from the Serbian side, VJ officer, and also later on this is also conversation between Colonel Ljubisa Beara and officer from VJ, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the screen we can see J, who is designated as Jevtic, saying to S: "We are catching some, and the MUP is too." Just before that, a few lines before that, you see S saying: "Listen, why do you let these Turks swim towards you?" J says: "They," as the interpreters indicate here, "float, and let them go on." Then he says: "Listen, we have some information that they are relocating across the river, man, not swimming." Does this correspond with your understanding of the circumstances or the events that are recorded in the intelligence report that is signed by Zoran Carkic, 65 ter 7510 that I just showed you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this corresponds to Zoran Carkic report or information, intelligence information about Muslim population from Zepa, that they are trying to cross the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could just go to the second page in the English and in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can see -- wait a minute. Third page, I'm sorry, in the English. Thanks. Right at the top of the page, here, we can see that Beara participates in this conversation, as you had previously indicated; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is Beara talking to Jevtic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with that, I would like to tender 65 ter 7510.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 7510 shall be assigned Exhibit P2606. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Blaszczyk, I would like to show you a couple of other documents. Let me show you 65 ter 6183.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I just note: I don't find it on the list of documents to be used during your examination, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I've been alerted to that. If you could just bear with me for one second, I will find the correct number. It's 4183. I apologise for that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise this document, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is combat order from the Drina Corps collection document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to show you, and if we could compare this, the B/C/S versions of it, is 65 ter 7528. And what can you tell us about 65 ter 7528? Where is it from?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to this document on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you go up a little bit? I believe this is document from the Pecanac collection, but I would like to check -- yes. Looking at the ERN number, I recognise this document as being from Pecanac collection, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this from the hard drive or from the CD?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is from the hard drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in fact this is copy of the same document we see on the left-hand side here, except handwritten text from the document from Pecanac collection is named Proboj, which is code-name of the operation, sweep operation, I think, in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go to the last page, it should be page 6, I think, in both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can see here a signature on the B/C/S. Can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is signature of the commander at that time of Drina Corps, General Milenko Zivanovic, but I think he was colonel at that time. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just so that we are clear, we are looking right now at 65 ter 4183. And now I see we've got -- we've got 7528 up on the right-hand side of the screen so we can compare the two signatures. And does this change or confirm your opinion that this is a copy?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It confirms my opinion. This is a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender both of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, first 65 ter 4183.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P2607. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As well as 65 ter 7528.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2608. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I'd like to show you just a couple of other documents. This one is 65 ter 7529. All right. I think we'll need the English translation we have. You see this is a 13 July 1995 report from the Main Staff of Republika Srpska. And have you had a chance to compare this document to other material within the collections of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. Vanderpuye said that the document is dated 13 July. I believe that he misspoke, because the date on the document is 13 January 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gajic. That is correct. I did misspeak. 13 January 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had opportunity to review these documents and also corroborating material.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. What I would like to do is what I've been doing, which is to show 65 ter 4866, which is the B/C/S version of a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number; it's not recorded correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It should be 4866.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to compare these two documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a chance. This is exactly the same contents of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I note that the type is different, type face.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the type is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we go to the second page of both documents, we see now another stamp, different from the red and the blue one we discussed earlier. Can you tell us about that one?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to which document, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the document on the right of the screen, 65 ter 4866, bears a stamp that is different than the document on the right-hand [sic] side of the screen which is 65 ter 7529.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is different stamp used by the subordinated unit of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then we have a signature on the document 7529. That's the document from the Pecanac collection. Are you familiar with that signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is signature of General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And comparing the text of these two documents, did you find any differences in the content?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the content is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would tender these two documents as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First, leave is granted to add 65 ter 7529 to your 65 ter exhibit list, and it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 7529 shall be assigned Exhibit P2609.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And then 65 ter 4866 will be received as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2610. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show you 65 ter 7530.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it, again, that there is no objection to add it to the exhibit list; therefore, leave is granted to do that. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe I could be of some assistance. There seems to be a problem. I can't find the document in e-court myself. It has either not been released or it has not been downloaded -- or uploaded, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry, there appears to be an anomaly. It's either -- Mr. Gajic is right, it doesn't seem to be available. But that won't stop me. I'll go to another document, if I may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's try with 65 ter 7531.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is document from Pecanac collection, from his hard drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the ERN number. This is an ERN range we stamp these documents from -- from the hard drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And we can see here that it refers to Krivaja 95, as we can see denoted at the top. It has a copy number indicated there, which maybe we can blow up. It's on the right-hand side of the screen. Are you able to read that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very hardly, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It looks like it says "Primerak."

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Were you able to compare that against any other document in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I compared these documents with other copy of Krivaja 95 document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could once again display in the B/C/S version side by side P1202.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to compare these two documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I had. And the same document with the same copy number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And having compared them, can you say whether or not they are photocopies or they are identical or different?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are identical. But this document on the right-hand side we -- I think we received from, if I am correct, from Ministry of Defence of RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you're able to tell that because of the ERN range, is it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, I'm looking at ERN range of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. But in any case that ERN --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am correct, because I'm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. But in any case, that ERN range does not correspond to the documents that were seized and processed and part of the Pecanac collection; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. It's totally different ERN range.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender these two documents as well, 65 ter 7531 -- oh, I'm sorry, just 65 ter 7531.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter document 7531 shall be assigned Exhibit P2611. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- I would like to squeeze one in just before the break, if I can. But if you want, we can take our break and I can come back. I have only a handful of documents, but I think I can actually cut it short because essentially it's the same process for each of them. So however you would like to proceed, is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It depends on the length of the remainder of your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then let's take our break then, and I will try and keep it short when we get back. Thanks, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have our second break now, and we will resume quater past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I may, can I have 65 ter 7294 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is this a document that comes also from the Pecanac collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. It comes from the first batch of DVDs we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in the top right-hand corner of the document, we can see some handwritten material. Have you had a chance to review that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had. I recognise here is, I believe, this is signature of General Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You said "signature"; what you are referring to specifically?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to is visible here as ZT, just the -- I mean initials, rather, yeah, exactly this is the initials of, I believe, General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And we can see here that this document refers to information that is being relayed by Captain Momir Nikolic, chief of security and intelligence of the Bratunac Brigade. And we can see that it's relayed to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, security administration. And it informs the Main Staff that the forces are in control of certain UN or UNPROFOR observation points. In particular, it refers to the UNPROFOR observation post in Biljeg. Have you had a chance to compare this document to other information concerning these circumstances in the OTP collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is to show you 65 ter 5893. This one will be sequential, so I won't need to show it side by side. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is document prepared by Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we see that it's dated 8 July 1995, like the previous document.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what about this document compares to the previous document that we saw?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you -- can we go back to the previous document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. It's 65 ter 7294.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I look at this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It will be coming up hopefully in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now you have both documents in B/C/S on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On the right-hand side, we have the document from Pecanac collection. I call it Pecanac collection. And the document from the left side, this is -- I believe this is the document from Drina Corps collection. And both documents are talking about the same -- the same events about UNPROFOR check-point in the place called Biljeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us something about the origin of the document on the left, 65 ter 5893. Does it come also from the Pecanac collection, or from another collection of documents in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I mentioned it, that these documents, I am referring to documents from my left-hand side now, with ERN number 0436-6610, this document comes from Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You will notice also that the document on the right is directed to the Drina Corps command and to the security administration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Is called -- this document is directed to the command of Drina Corps, security administration; also to the Main Staff of Republika Srpska Army, security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the -- would it make sense, then, that the document on the left, which is 65 ter 5893, reflecting the same information, would be -- would have been issued by Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. And we see that document on the right-hand side, this document was sent exactly originate -- I mean, received by headquarters in Crna Rijeka. I see the stamp of the communication unit from Crna Rijeka and also the name of one of the cryptographer, his name is Vukajlovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to tender these two documents, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 65 ter 7294 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And shall be assigned Exhibit P2612. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the other one, 65 ter 5893, will be received, too.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And shall be assigned Exhibit P2613. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, I have one more document to show you, and that's 65 ter 2590A. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I was inquiring if there was an English translation of it, and I see there is not. So let me go -- let me come at this document from the other side, which would be if I put up 65 ter 2590 instead of 2590A. I think this version has a translation. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we can see here that this is a document from the command of the Drina Corps, security and intelligence department. 13 July 1995 is its date. And it's sent to the Main Staff security and intelligence sector, and it says "intelligence administration." If we go to the bottom of the document in the B/C/S and page 2 in the English, we'll see that it was sent by the chief of the intelligence and security department. It says lieutenant-colonel, and it doesn't have a name. All right. Have you had a chance to compare this document to the documents in the Pecanac collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And we can see in this document that the chief of intelligence and security department in the Drina Corps is relaying information concerning the movement of Muslim prisoners, and that's quite throughout the document. Now, if I can show you 65 ter 2590A and compare that to 65 ter 2590, just the B/C/S, side by side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I note, Mr. Vanderpuye, that the letter 65 ter 2590A is not included in your list of documents to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's true. You're right. I apologise for that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, we have in e-court before us on the left side of the screen 65 ter 2590, and on the right, 65 ter 2590A. First let me ask you: The document on the left, ERN 0359-1071, can you tell us where that document came from? What's its origin?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is document from the command of the Drina Corps, sector for intelligence, I believe, and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: From what collection does this come from in the possession of the OTP, if you know?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise the number, the range, the ERN number now, but I think it is quite old document, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the document, the document on the right, 65 ter 2590 -- 2590A, from where does that document come, what collection can it be found in?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitively is document from so-called Pecanac collection from his CDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to compare the two documents in terms of their substance and content?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And the content of these documents is the same, like the -- another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can we go to the bottom of the page in both documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Again we have -- we have a difference in the type of stamp that we have in the document on the right and the document on the left. And is your explanation for that the same as it has been with respect to the other documents with similar stamps?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say that this document from Pecanac collection on the right-hand side, this is document, in fact, which finally ended up in the Main Staff in Crna Rijeka, because I see the stamp used by the communication officer from Crna Rijeka. And it says here "received." This means that they received this information from Drina Corps, I believe. And on the left-hand side document, this is not clear here, but this is stamp of one of the subordinated unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And we can see on the right-hand side 65 ter 6 -- 2590A, I'm sorry, we can see that that document is in a different kind of type-face than the one on the left. Does that indicate that the document on the right -- is that a sent or a received stamp on it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's different type of typewriting here, yes. In the stamp it says "received," but it could be also received for sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we go to the top of the document, again we see different handwritten entries on the document. And is your explanation for that the same as it has been with respect to the other documents we've looked at with different handwriting portions of it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. I'm convinced now that this document on the right-hand side, it was received by the Main Staff, sector for intelligence and security. And the handwritings here on the right document is totally different than on the left-hand side. It's visible here. And also I see indication that that document was -- this is the number of intelligence department from the Main Staff, 12/45.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And for the record, that's in the centre of the top of the document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. But I'm not sure about initials on this document, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are referring to the document on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. Mr. President, I would like to tender these two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Both documents will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 2590A shall be assigned Exhibit P2614. And 65 ter document 2590 shall be assigned Exhibit P2615. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just one last question: Mr. Blaszczyk, in your review of the documents from the Pecanac collection and comparison to the documents that are in other collections of the OTP, did you come across documents that had any indication in the Pecanac collection that had they been tampered with or suggested in any way that they had been manipulated or altered in any way?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that. I review most of these documents from this collection, and I don't remember. I didn't notice any such document that could be tampered or altered in somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe that they would have been?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. And we are referring to these type of the documents, mostly the JPEG files, as I said, not to PDF files or Word documents, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That concludes my direct examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. One issue remains open. We have just received the two documents with the number 2590, and that one with an A has no English translation. Are you going to ask for an English translation or what are your intentions?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't think one is necessary, Mr. President, because -- I don't think one's necessary, so no. I don't intend to ask for a translation, unless the Defence requires and then I'll do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The content of both documents seems to be the same. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the contents are the same in the biggest parts. The only difference is in the stamps at the bottom of the two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And, of course, in the handwriting. Therefore, I think there's no need for another translation of the body of the document. Thank you very much, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, now it's your turn to commence your cross-examination. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm glad I can welcome Mr. Blaszczyk to this courtroom, and I would like to thank him for come here to testify in these proceedings and to talk about the documents. The Defence has no questions for him and basically this brings our cross-examination to an end. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. In that case, there will be no re-examination, of course. Mr. Blaszczyk, thank you very much that you were able to come to this trial again. Now you, again, are free to return to your normal work with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may leave the courtroom. All the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I see you on your feet. We have to deal with your next days and the scheduling of witnesses. There was and there is one witness scheduled for tomorrow, but there is some uncertainty if he will be able the testify tomorrow, if he will be here in The Hague. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. President. May we go into private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have discussed during the private period of our hearings the further scheduling of witnesses. Tomorrow there will be no hearing, that will be cancelled. On Thursday, in two weeks' [sic] time, we will resume our hearings at 10.30 in the morning for a videolink. We resume in Courtroom III. Now we adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
